Explanation: Cycle time is the total time it takes for a unit of work to be completed, from the beginning to the end of a process. Includes all stages of processing and delays
Examples: Cycle time: the total time it takes for one case (e.g., a customer order, a patient treatment) to go through the entire process from start to finish.
Goal - Parameter Relation Example: “Reduce cycle time” → shorten activity durations or change their distributions.

Explanation: time spent actively working on a task or activity.
Examples:
Healthcare: Lab test takes 30 minutes.
Logistics: Shipment check takes 10 minutes.

Explanation:
how unexpected things happen in the process
occurrence of start/catching events
Examples:
Patients frequently leave the ER without being treated if waiting > 90 minutes.

Explanation: Likelihood of branching at XOR/OR decision points
Examples:
Insurance: 70% claims go straight to approval, 30% require manual review.
Healthcare: 50% patients discharged, 30% need radiology, 20% go to surgery.
Goal - Parameter Relation Example: “Change routing logic to balance load across departments.”

Explanation: The actual individual workers, machines, or units
Responsible for performing each activity in the process model
Grouping of resources with similar skills/capabilities
Examples:
Hospital: Nurse role vs. Doctor role
Call center: Agent role vs. “Supervisor role
Goal - Parameter Relation Example: “Ensure flexible allocation of staff” → adjust role definitions.

Explanation: Default working times for a role, availability schedules
Examples: Nurses available 24/7 in shifts, but radiology only Mon–Fri 9–17h.
Goal - Parameter Relation Example: “Match resources to demand” → extend shifts, add night coverage.

Explanation: How much a resource costs to employ
Goal - Parameter Relation Example: “Reduce cost per patient” → substitute expensive roles where possible.

Explanation: how many cases/runs the simulation should execute
Examples:
patients, orders, calls, etc. - 
Healthcare: Simulate 1,000 patients arriving at an ER to test how bottlenecks form.
Manufacturing: Simulate 500 production orders in a month to compare throughput.
Goal - Parameter Relation Example: “Check scalability of process under increased demand” → Increase number of simulated instances.

Parameter: Cycle time, Waiting + Processing + Inter waiting times + Off timetable
The actual working or processing time spent on value-adding activities (without waiting or idle periods).
The time an entity spends waiting for resources or the next activity before processing continues.
The deviation from the scheduled time (how much earlier or later than planned an activity or appointment occurred).
